historical_growth.owner_fcf_basis: OCF - capex - lease payments - SBC (unlevered; TP's OCF excludes interest). Lease payments FY2019-FY2025: 208, 212, 218, 244, 261, 311, 315 (annual URD cash-flow statements). Pre-FY2019 years omitted: IFRS 16 adoption in FY2019 moved lease principal out of OCF, so OCF/EBITDA before and after are not comparable.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Not a historical CAGR. Average of the base-case 10-year reported-revenue path, anchored to FY2026 guidance (0-2% LFL, ~-2.5% reported after FX) and the 2028 target (4-6% LFL) haircut to 3%. Historical CAGRs are M&A-driven (Majorel, Nov-2023, added ~EUR 2bn of revenue; FY2024 revenue +23%) and pre-date the 2024-2026 AI de-rating; FY2025 revenue -0.7% and owner FCF -19% from the FY2024 peak. Extrapolating them would be the naive error this build is designed to avoid.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 3.7% vs revenue 7.8% and EPS -7.9%: divergence >30%. Equity growth is depressed by EUR 708m of FY2025 translation losses and EUR 97m impairment; EPS fell on higher financing cost and amortization post-Majorel while revenue grew by acquisition. None of the three is a usable forward growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (14.9% 3yr) exceeds reported-FCF CAGR (11.6%) because SBC FELL from 113m (FY2022) to 77m (FY2025) - the reverse of the usual SBC-outgrowing-cash warning. Both are flattered by the Majorel acquisition; the organic signal is FY2024 -> FY2025 owner FCF -19% (1,192 -> 969) and H1-2026 net FCF of 243m vs 259m.

scenario_narratives.base: Transition year then grind. FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance (-2.5% reported after FX, 18.3% owner EBITDA after EUR 120-140m restructuring), FY2027-28 returns to 2-3% growth as AI-powered solutions, back-office and Data Services for AI scale past the shrinking Trust & Safety and voice-seat base. Margins settle near 19.5% - flat on FY2025 - because the Future Forward savings are consumed by AI investment and by restructuring that recurs every year. Owner FCF ~EUR 830m in FY2026 rising to ~EUR 1.1bn by FY2035; 12x exit, a partial recovery from today's ~9.5x.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-integrator thesis works: the 2028 plan is delivered in full (4-6% LFL, 15.5% EBITA), transformation mega-contracts sign, the portfolio review prunes Trust & Safety, leases shrink with offshoring. TP re-rates from AI casualty to AI distributor for 1,500 enterprise clients at 14x FCF - still below its 2015-2021 multiple. Owner FCF ~EUR 1.5bn by FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bear: Agentic AI does to voice and chat what it already did to Trust & Safety: tier-1 volumes are automated or in-sourced, per-interaction pricing deflates faster than offshoring can offset, revenue shrinks ~3%/yr for a decade, operating deleverage and perpetual restructuring compress owner EBITDA to 14%, and the EUR 4bn debt stack absorbs a growing share of a falling cash flow. 10x exit on ~EUR 400m of FCF, no re-rating.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Teleperformance is valued as a leveraged, low-growth services cash flow whose central question is survival of the human-agent model against agentic AI, not its growth rate. The build therefore (1) anchors FY2026 to guidance rather than to any historical CAGR, all of which are Majorel-inflated; (2) treats TP's 'non-recurring' restructuring as a recurring owner cost, because it has been booked in every year since 2023 and is guided higher for 2026; (3) charges leases once as an operating cost and keeps lease liabilities out of net debt; (4) uses one 8% EUR WACC across scenarios and prices the AI-disruption risk in a 35% bear weight and a bear path that halves owner FCF; (5) caps exit multiples at 10-14x, below the house 20x, so the valuation does not depend on the stock recovering its pre-2022 rating. The weighted value above the current price is a statement that the market is pricing something close to the bear path as its central case, not that the base case is safe.
key_risks_to_valuation: Agentic AI substitutes human agents faster than TP can redeploy its 490,000-person workforce into AI-powered, back-office and data services - the bear path, or worse
FY2026 guidance miss: H2-2026 must deliver ~+3-4% LFL and a 15.5%+ H2 EBITA margin for the full-year 14.6% and EUR 800-850m FCF to hold; TP missed in 2024 and the stock halved
Restructuring that is never non-recurring: FY2026 guidance was raised 70-90m -> 120-140m within four months; the base assumes 0.6% of revenue in perpetuity, the bear more

Leverage: EUR 4.0bn IFRS net debt (3.2bn ex-lease), 2.1x EBITDA, bonds refinanced at 4.75-5.375%; a bear-path EBITDA decline would push leverage toward 3x and threaten the BBB rating and the EUR 4.50 dividend
New external CEO (March 2026) with no P&L record at TP executing a strategic portfolio review that could involve dilutive or value-destructive M&A/disposals; no acquisition spend is modelled
FX: EUR strength vs USD/INR/GBP cut H1-2026 revenue by EUR 165m; reported growth paths assume FX laps by FY2027
Terminal cap multiple is the largest single lever: each 1x on the base cap is worth ~EUR 8-9/share; at a 10x base cap (no re-rating at all) the base value falls by roughly EUR 17/share
Price volatility: the stock is at its 52-week high after an ~85% rally from the 2026 low with >12% short interest; the entry-price discipline matters more than usual

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com, TEP.PA) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 43.65-80.58 EUR.
data_sources.financials: TEP.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt (Universal Registration Document 2025: income statement 14690-14713, cash-flow statement 14741-14775, APM reconciliations 2515-2597, Group cash flows 2808-2828); TEP.PA_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (cash-flow statement 190-224, treasury shares and EPS 771-795, net debt roll 1152-1170, APM reconciliations 1286-1371); lease payments FY2019-FY2023 from the FY2020-FY2023 URD cash-flow statements; TEP.PA_Metrics.csv via make dcf-context (metrics_normalized, EUR millions).
data_sources.qualitative: TEP.PA_Analysis.json (2026-10-26): business model, AI-disruption risk, Future Forward plan, FY2026 guidance and 2026-2028 objectives, March 2026 leadership transition, May 2026 bond refinancing.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 59,874,365 shares in issue less 1,740,734 treasury/own shares (160,117 liquidity contract + 1,580,617 own shares, H1-2026 note 6.2) = 58.13m outstanding, plus ~0.26m dilutive performance-share awards (H1-2026 note 6.3 diluted weighted average 58,399,903). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Financial net debt EXCLUDING lease liabilities, 30 June 2026: reported IFRS net debt EUR 4,013m (H1-2026 note 8.4) less lease liabilities EUR 801m (601 non-current + 200 current) = EUR 3,212m. Cash and equivalents EUR 1,027m (net cash EUR 1,020m after EUR 7m overdrafts). Lease liabilities are excluded because the full lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 unlevered, pre-SBC owner base: net cash flow from operating activities 1,614 (TP's OCF excludes all interest paid/received) less capex 253 less lease payments 315 = 1,046. TP's own 'net free cash flow' (post net interest paid of 183) was EUR 870m, EUR 901m excluding non-recurring cash-outs; the Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow of 1,361 is OCF - capex before lease payments. last_fcf = 1,046 - 77 SBC = 969 (unlevered, post-lease, post-SBC, at levered cash tax of 380). The component build's FY2025-equivalent at an unlevered 33% cash tax is ~EUR 925-945m; the ~EUR 50m gap is the interest tax shield, which the WACC carries.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated income statement line 'Share-based payments' EUR 77m (TEP.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:14697; FY2024 91m). TP settles performance-share plans with treasury shares; no net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed, so the P&L charge is the combined figure. H1-2026 charge was only EUR 15m (vs 45m) after forfeitures on the March 2026 founder/deputy-CEO departures.
inputs.interest_income_note: Income from cash and equivalents was EUR 27m in FY2025 but it sits below operating profit and TP's OCF excludes interest received, so it is already outside the FCF base and the component build; nothing to strip. The cash pile is credited once, in the net-debt bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity outflow 'Acquisition net of disposal of treasury shares' EUR 114m (FY2024 184m; FY2023 366m). H1-2026: nil. The flat count is being funded by actual repurchases plus treasury-share settlement of awards; FY2026 dividend EUR 4.50/share (EUR 262m paid H1-2026) is the primary return channel.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:39Z regular close (Euronext Paris Friday close; the Monday 2026-10-26 session had not printed on Yahoo at build time). Price sits at the 52-week high after a ~85% rally off the 2026 low.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows: 10y Bund risk-free ~2.8%, equity risk premium 5.5%, equity beta 1.4 (de-rated, >12% short interest, leveraged services cyclical) -> cost of equity ~10.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.2% (May-2026 bonds at 4.75%/5.375%, S&P BBB stable), ~3.6% after a 30% marginal rate. Weights at market: equity ~60% (market cap ~EUR 4.7bn), debt ~40% (ex-lease net debt EUR 3.2bn) -> 7.7%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: AI-disruption, leverage and leadership risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and the probability weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, cash-flow statement 'Lease payments': FY2025 EUR 315m = 3.1% of revenue; H1-2026 EUR 163m = 3.3%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (EUR 801m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. EBITDA margin path is TP's 'EBITDA before non-recurring items' basis (pre-SBC, pre-lease-depreciation), so the lease is charged exactly once. D&A for cash tax (da_pct_path 2.6%) is depreciation and amortization EX right-of-use depreciation (EUR 268m FY2025) and EX amortization of acquired intangibles (EUR 218m, non-cash and treated as non-deductible), so the lease is not charged a second time through D&A.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are nil (net profit attributable to NCI is blank in FY2025 and H1-2026; NCI equity EUR 5-6m). No adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, non-US and cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Teleperformance is a BPO/CX outsourcer with contractual but volume-sensitive revenue; its value is a stream of free cash flow, so the owner-FCF engine applies. Not a financial, REIT or LIC. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). EBITDA BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is TP's 'EBITDA before non-recurring items' (FY2025 EUR 1,990m = 19.5%; 2,006m = 19.6% excluding the EUR 16m Majorel-synergy/French-reorganisation cost) LESS the restructuring and 'non-recurring' costs TP strips, which an owner pays every year (FY2024 115m, FY2025 38m, FY2026 guided 120-140m + EUR 109m already booked in H1-2026). FY2025 on this owner basis: 1,990 - 22 other operating expenses = 1,968 = 19.3%. FY2026 guidance (recurring EBITA ~14.6% = recurring EBITDA ~19.7% after adding back 2.6% D&A and 2.5% ROU depreciation) less 1.3% restructuring and 0.1% other = 18.3% is the Y1 base anchor. FY0/HORIZON: FY0 = FY2025 (last full year; revenue 10,209), Y1 = FY2026 (the guidance year, 10 months elapsed at valuation), 10-year explicit horizon because bear margins are still compressing and base margins still ramping at year 5. Balance sheet and share count are from 30 June 2026, four months newer than FY0, so H1-2026 FCF (EUR 243m net) and the FY2025 dividend (EUR 262m) are already in net debt; the Y1 flow is therefore slightly double-counted for one half-year, worth under EUR 2/share. REVENUE: growth paths are REPORTED EUR growth, not LFL. FY2026 LFL guidance 0-2% translates to about -2.5% reported after the EUR 165m H1 FX drag (EUR strength vs USD/INR/GBP) and TLScontact visa-contract non-renewal; H1-2026 reported was -4.5% (LFL -1.7%). WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-8%): a receivables-heavy services business consumes cash when it grows and releases it when it shrinks (FY2025: revenue -71m, WC +52m; H1-2026: WC -29m). TERMINAL: cap multiples 10x/12x/14x bear/base/bull, below the 20x house default, for a structurally challenged, low-growth services business; today's EV/owner-FCF is ~9.5x, so the base cap assumes a modest re-rating from the AI-fear trough and the bear assumes none. SIGNIFICANT ITEMS: FY2025 included a EUR 97m goodwill/intangible impairment (non-cash, excluded) and EUR 454m of acquisitions (ZP Better Together, Agents Only) excluded from the FCF base as inorganic; no acquisition spend is projected, consistent with the Board's stated portfolio-review/pruning stance.

bear.narrative: Agentic AI does to voice and chat seats what it is already doing to Trust & Safety: clients in-source or automate tier-1 contact volumes, pricing per interaction deflates faster than TP can offshore, and the AI-powered lines grow but from too small a base. Reported revenue shrinks ~3% a year for a decade (to ~EUR 7.6bn), operating deleverage on a 70%-labour cost base and perpetual restructuring take owner EBITDA from 19.3% to 14%, and the EUR 4bn debt stack (refinanced at 4.75-5.4%) absorbs a rising share of a falling cash flow. No re-rating: 10x exit on ~EUR 400m of FCF. The genuine tail - a Klarna-style collapse in human-agent demand - sits below this path and is why the bear weight is raised, not why the bear path itself is made catastrophic.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 FY2026 -2.5% reported: guidance 0-2% LFL less ~3pp FX (EUR 165m drag in H1 alone) and the TLScontact visa non-renewal; H1 actual -4.5% reported, H2 needs ~+1% reported. Y2 +2% as FX laps and AI-powered/back-office lines (double-digit growth) offset Trust & Safety decline. Y3-Y5 +3%: management targets 4-6% LFL in 2028; the base gives them half, reflecting AI pricing deflation on commoditised voice/chat work. Taper to 2% by Y8, below nominal GDP.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 owner-basis EBITDA 19.3% (1,990 before non-recurring less 22 other operating expenses). Y1 18.3% = guided recurring EBITDA ~19.7% less 1.3% of guided restructuring (EUR 120-140m) treated as a real cost. Recurring margin then climbs toward the 2028 target (15.5% EBITA = ~20.6% EBITDA) but the base credits only ~20.1% and keeps a 0.6% permanent restructuring charge: 19.5% from Y5. Net effect: essentially flat vs FY2025; management's margin expansion is consumed by the restructuring it requires.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2025 capex 253 (2.5%) below ex-ROU D&A 268 (2.6%); H1-2026 capex 96 (2.0%). Capex rises to 2.7% from Y3 as TP.ai FAB / AI platform spend replaces seat capex; D&A held at 2.6%. Lease cost 3.2% (FY2025 3.1%, H1-2026 3.3%).
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax rate on unlevered EBIT (ex acquired-intangible amortization): FY2025 cash taxes paid 380 vs owner EBIT ~1,308 less net interest 211 = 34.6% levered; the ~2pp uplift for the interest shield makes 33% the unlevered equivalent. Eases to 32% from Y5 as impairment-related non-deductibles fade. Never credited on a loss (engine applies max(0, EBIT)).
base.terminal_rationale: g 1.5%, below ECB 2% inflation, for a business whose unit pricing is deflating. Cap 12x FCF: Gordon at 8%/1.5% would be 15.6x, which no buyer has paid for a BPO since 2022; today's EV/owner-FCF is ~9.5x, so 12x assumes partial recovery from the AI-fear trough but not a return to the 15-20x of 2015-2021.
base.narrative: Transition year then grind: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance, FY2027-28 return to low-single-digit LFL growth as AI-powered solutions, back-office and Data Services for AI scale past the shrinking Trust & Safety and voice-seat base; margins hold near 19.5% because the Future Forward savings (>EUR 100m run-rate) are reinvested in AI and in the restructuring that never quite becomes non-recurring. Owner FCF ~EUR 830m in FY2026 rising to ~EUR 1.1bn by FY2035.

bull.narrative: The AI-integrator thesis works: management delivers the 2028 plan in full (4-6% LFL, 15.5% EBITA = ~20.6% recurring EBITDA, with restructuring fading to ~0.2%), one or two of the 'hundreds of millions of euros' transformation contracts sign, the portfolio review prunes Trust & Safety, and the lease footprint shrinks with offshoring and work-from-home. The stock re-rates from AI casualty to AI distributor for 1,500 enterprise clients; a 14x FCF exit is still below its 2015-2021 range. Owner FCF reaches ~EUR 1.5bn by FY2035.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 35/45/20. Bear raised to 35%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (labour-arbitrage BPO to AI integrator) under a brand-new external CEO, the dominant risk is structural rather than cyclical, and the evidence is mixed in real time (Trust & Safety shrinking, Q1/H1-2026 LFL negative, restructuring guidance raised from 70-90m to 120-140m within four months). Leverage of 2.1x EBITDA with recently refinanced higher coupons removes the balance-sheet cushion that would otherwise justify a lower bear weight. Bull cut to 20%: it needs several independent things to go right - full delivery of the 2028 margin target, mega-contract signings, successful portfolio pruning AND a market re-rating. Base at 45% is management's plan with a haircut, which is where the H1-2026 evidence (stable 13.6% recurring EBITA, reaffirmed FY guidance, AI lines growing double-digit) actually points.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
